title: A Podcast on Returning to School as an Adult
script: Host: [warmly] Welcome back to the show. Today my guest is Andi, who went back to university at twenty-eight after years of working. Thanks for joining me.
Guest: [pleasantly] Thank you for having me. I still feel a little strange calling myself a student again.
Host: [curious] What made you decide to go back to school after so long?
Guest: [thoughtful] I worked in a warehouse for years, and I wanted a job with more stability, so I chose to study logistics management.
Host: [interested] Was it difficult to sit in a classroom again after being away for so long?
Guest: [honestly] Extremely difficult, especially the first month. I felt slower than the younger students, and my memory felt rusty.
Host: [sympathetically] Did you ever consider quitting during that first month?
Guest: [reflective] Almost every day, actually. But I kept thinking about my daughter, and I wanted her to see me finish something hard.
Host: [curious] How did you manage studying while also working part time?
Guest: [gently] I studied early in the morning, before my shift, when the house was quiet and my mind was still fresh.
Host: [interested] What surprised you most about being an older student?
Guest: [warmly] Honestly, the younger students were kind. Several of them helped me with computer skills I had never used before.
Host: [curious] Do you think age was actually a disadvantage in the classroom?
Guest: [thoughtful] Less than I expected. I was slower with technology, but I understood work and responsibility better than some classmates.
Host: [curious] What would you tell someone your age who is scared to go back to school?
Guest: [encouraging] I would say the fear never fully disappears, but it gets smaller every single week you keep showing up.
Host: [smiling] That's wonderful advice, Andi. Thank you for sharing your story with us today.
Guest: [warmly] Thank you for listening. I hope it helps someone finally register for that class they keep postponing.
